newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda accuses Sudanese planes of bombing north.
newsitem.headline: Uganda accuses Sudanese planes of bombing north.

text.p: The Ugandan government on Friday accused Sudanese warplanes of twice bombing northern Uganda on Thursday, saying they wounded eight people.
Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi said in a statement that an Antonov transport plane, which Khartoum uses as a bomber, and a MiG jet violated Ugandan airspace late on Thursday afternoon.
"They tried to bomb Moyo army barracks but missed the target. Three civilians and one child were injured. Five bombs which fell near the barracks did not explode," Mbabazi said.

"Later last night at about nine o'clock another military aircraft of Antonov type again entered from Sudan via Koboko and Arua and dropped bombs, wounding one person seriously and three other persons sustaining minor injuries," he added.
He said Ugandan army anti-aircraft batteries fired at the Sudanese planes but they were flying too high out of range.
"We condemn in the strongest terms this act of aggression which was clearly not provoked. Uganda reserves the right to retaliate appropriately," Mbabazi said without elaborating.
Ugandas government last accused a Sudanese plane of violating its airspace on February 3.
Independent sources have confirmed Sudanese planes have bombed northern Uganda several times in the past two years but Khartoum denies doing so or says the attacks were unintentional.
Khartoum accuses Uganda of backing the Sudan Peoples Liberation Army, which has been fighting since 1983 in the mainly Christian and animist south against the Moslem, Arabised north.
In turn, Uganda accuses Sudan of supporting rebel movements in northern and western Uganda. Both countries deny the charges.
